title: Adaptive kernel gating and decode-smoothing for FlashAttention compatibility
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Summary:
We observed intermittent latency and memory regressions when enabling FlashAttention v3 on mixed-input production traces. This ticket implements an adaptive kernel gating layer and a decode-smoothing policy that together: (1) route requests to the most appropriate attention kernel at request-time based on lightweight fingerprints and telemetry; (2) reduce decode jitter by pacing the prefill->decode transition and applying microtiling fallbacks for pathological long-context shapes.

Goals:
- Prevent v3 regressions from impacting tail latency and OOMs for long-context workloads.
- Maintain v3 fast-path for common short/medium contexts to preserve throughput/cost gains.
- Provide safe, observable staged rollout and automated fallback logic so customer traffic stays within SLOs.

Design highlights:
- Lightweight fingerprinting: compute a compact signature for (batch_size, seq_len_prefill, seq_len_decode, model_variant, quant_mode). Use this to query a small in-memory scoring table (LRU cache) that stores preferred kernel + confidence.
- Probabilistic gating: when confidence low, do an asynchronous micro-probe to both v2 and v3 fast-paths on a subset of warmup requests and update scores. Default to conservative kernel for first N requests per fingerprint to avoid oscillation.
- Decode-smoothing: instead of instant handoff from prefill to decode kernel, apply a 3-stage transition (prefill-only, hybrid decode with X% microbatching, full decode) spread over a configurable warmup window per fingerprint to reduce workspace thrash and KV cache churn.
- Microtiling fallback: expose a compact workspace-reduction parameter to v3 kernels for long contexts; fall back to v2 or tiled v3 variant when workspace budget exceeds threshold.
- Policy controls: operator flags for aggressive/neutral/conservative modes, per-customer overrides (Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in by default).

Telemetry and metrics to add:
- kernel_choice_count{kernel=v2|v3|tiled}
- kernel_probe_success_rate
- probe_latency_delta_ms
- prefill_to_decode_transition_ms (quantiles)
- workspace_alloc_failures
- canary_failure_rate (by customer)
- scoring_table_hit_rate

Implementation plan:
1) RFC + config proto (this ticket) - small in-memory scorer and gating state machine.
2) Instrumentation hooks: add per-request fingerprint generation and a light-weight scoring lookup in the serving hotpath.
3) Micro-prober: non-blocking background probe harness that runs paired kernels for sampled fingerprints and records latency/memory deltas to telemetry.
4) Decode-smoother: implement staged transition logic in the runtime's scheduler with knobs for warmup window and microbatch percentage.
5) Canary: rollout to internal canary region + selected low-risk customers. Add automatic rollback if 95p latency increases > 15% or OOMs spike.
6) Gradual expansion with telemetry-driven policy updates and a migration job to pre-seed scoring table for high-volume fingerprints.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for scorer/LRU behavior and gating FSM.
- Integration tests running mixed prefill/decode traces from production replay (short, medium, long contexts).
- Stress test on A100 and H100 shapes with quantized models to validate workspace budgets.
- Fleet canary with runtime-1.20: compare metrics against baseline for 48h before expanding.

Rollout and safety:
- Default mode: conservative (prefer v2 for unknown fingerprints).
- Canary rule: fail if workspace_alloc_failures > 0.1% or 95p latency regression > 15% over baseline.
- Operator override: ability to pin kernel choice per-customer or per-route via config.

Open trade-offs and decisions needed:
- Memory vs latency: aggressive prefetch/probing reduces uncertainty faster but increases short-term memory pressure — proposal is to keep probes sampled and non-blocking.
- Scoring TTL: how long to trust a fingerprint score when model versions or infra change? Proposal: score TTL = 24h with decay on model rollout.
- Observability budget: adding many new metrics increases cardinality—plan to roll high-cardinality metrics to a lower retention pipeline.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atl/confluence/display/RUNTIME/Adaptive+Kernel+Gating+RFC
- PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13258 (initial scorer + hooks)
- PR (scheduler): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13299 (decode-smoother + tests)
- Canary dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/rt-kernel-gating/canary-overview
- Prod replay traces (internal GDrive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Z-kernel-replay-2025

Success criteria:
- No customer-facing regressions during canary phase (meet canary failure thresholds).
- 10-20% reduction in v3-triggered OOMs for long-context workloads in conservative mode compared to previous rollout.
- Measurable preservation of v3 throughput for short contexts (within 5% of previous v3-only baseline).
